cues.en: Hey Vsauce, Michael here. There's a famous way to seemingly create chocolate out of nothing. Maybe you've seen it before. This chocolate bar is four squares by eight squares. But if you cut it like this, and then like this, and finally like this, you can rearrange the pieces like so and wind up with the same four by eight bar, but with a leftover piece apparently created
cues.zh: 嗨，Vsauce，我是 Michael。有一种广为人知的技巧，看似能凭空变出巧克力。也许你以前见过。这块巧克力是四乘八格的。但如果你像这样切开，再这样切，最后这样切，你就能像这样重新拼起来，得到一块同样四乘八的巧克力，而且还多出来一块，简直就像是

cues.en: out of thin air. There's a popular animation of this illusion as well. I call it an illusion because it's just that. Fake. In reality, the final bar is a bit smaller. It contains this much less chocolate. Each square along the cut is shorter than it was in the original, but the cut makes it difficult to notice right away. The animation is extra misleading because it tries to cover up its deception.
cues.zh: 凭空变出来的。关于这个视觉错觉，网上也有一个很火的动画。我之所以叫它错觉，是因为它确实只是障眼法。假的。实际上，拼完后的巧克力会稍微小一点点。它少了这么多巧克力。沿着切口的那几格都比原来要短一些，但斜着切让你很难立刻察觉到。那个动画更是误导人，因为它试图掩盖这个骗局。

cues.en: the lost height of each square is surreptitiously added in while the piece moves to make it hard to notice. I mean, come on, obviously you cannot cut up a chocolate bar and rearrange the pieces into more than you started with. Or can you? One of the strangest theorems in modern mathematics is the Banach-Tarski Paradox. It proves that there is in fact a way to take an object and
cues.zh: 每一格减少的高度，都在碎片移动时被偷偷补了回去，让你更难发现。拜托，很显然，你不可能把一块巧克力切碎再重新拼起来，得到的却比原来还多。还是说，其实可以？现代数学中最离奇的定理之一就是巴拿赫-塔斯基悖论（Banach-Tarski Paradox）。它证明了，事实上确实有一种方法可以把一个物体

cues.en: separate it into five different pieces. And then, with those five pieces, simply rearrange them. No stretching required into two exact copies of the original item. Same density, same size, same everything. Seriously.
cues.zh: 切分成五块不同的碎片。然后，仅凭这五块碎片，直接重新拼合。完全不需要拉伸，就能变成两个和原来一模一样的一对复制品。密度相同，尺寸相同，一切都一模一样。说真的。

cues.en: To dive into the mind blow that it is, and the way it fundamentally questions math and ourselves, we have to start by asking a few questions. First, what is infinity? A number? I mean, it's nowhere on the number line, but we often say things like, there's an infinite number of blah blah blah. And as far as we know, infinity could be real.
cues.zh: 要领略这种震撼，以及它如何从根本上质疑数学乃至我们自身，我们得先提出几个问题。首先，什么是无限？是一个数字吗？在数轴上根本找不到它，但我们又经常说“有无限个某某某”。而据我们所知，无限可能是真实存在的。

cues.en: The universe may be infinite in size and flat, extending out forever and ever without end, beyond even the part we can observe or ever hope to observe. That's exactly what infinity is. Not a number per se, but rather a size. The size of something that doesn't end. Infinity is not the biggest number. Instead, it is how many numbers there are.
cues.zh: 宇宙的尺寸可能就是无限且平坦的，永无止境地向外延伸，甚至超越了我们能观测到、或有望观测到的范围。这就是无限的本质。它本身不是一个数字，而是一种规模。一种永无止境之物的规模。无限并不是最大的数字。相反，它是“有多少个数字”的度量。

cues.en: but there are different sizes of infinity. The smallest type of infinity is countable infinity, the number of hours in forever. It's also the number of whole numbers that there are, natural numbers, the numbers we use when counting things like 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and so on. Sets like these are unending, but they are countable. Countable means that you can count them
cues.zh: 但无限也是有不同大小的。最小的一种无限是“可数无限”，就像永恒之中包含的小时数。它也是所有整数、自然数的数量，也就是我们数数时用的数字，比如 1、2、3、4、5、6 等等。像这样的集合是无止境的，但它们是可数的。可数的意思是，你可以

cues.en: from one element to any other in a finite amount of time. Even if that finite amount of time is longer than you will live or the universe will exist for, it's still finite. Uncountable infinity, on the other hand, is literally bigger. Too big to even count. The number of real numbers that there are, not just whole numbers, but all numbers, is uncountably infinite.
cues.zh: 在有限的时间内，从其中一个元素数到另一个元素。即便这个有限时间比你的寿命、甚至比宇宙的存在时间还要长，它依然是有限的。而另一方面，“不可数无限”则是字面意义上的更大。大到根本无法去数。实数的数量——不仅仅是整数，而是所有数字的总和——就是不可数无限的。

cues.en: You literally cannot count even from 0 to 1 in a finite amount of time by naming every real number in between. I mean, where do you even start? 0. Okay, but what comes next? 0.00000. Eventually, we would imagine a 1 going somewhere at the end, but there is no end. We could always add another 0.
cues.zh: 你根本无法在有限时间内，通过逐一念出中间每一个实数，从 0 数到 1。我的意思是，你甚至从哪儿开始？0。好，那下一个是什么？0.00000。最终我们会想象末尾某处有个 1，但根本没有末尾。我们总能再加一个 0。

cues.en: Uncountability makes this set so much larger than the set of all whole numbers that even between 0 and 1 there are more numbers than there are whole numbers on the entire endless number line. Derricantor's famous diagonal argument helps illustrate this. Imagine listing every number between 0 and 1.
cues.zh: 不可数性使这个集合比所有整数的集合大得多，以至于仅在 0 和 1 之间，数字就比整条无尽数轴上的所有整数还多。Derricantor 著名的对角线论证有助于说明这一点。想象把 0 和 1 之间的每个数都列出来。

cues.en: Since they are uncountable and can't be listed in order, let's imagine randomly generating them forever with no repeats. Each number we generate can be paired with a whole number. If there's a one-to-one correspondence between the two, that is if we can match one whole number to each real number on our list, that would mean that countable and uncountable sets are the same size. But we can't do that.
cues.zh: 由于它们不可数，无法按顺序列出，我们不妨想象永远随机生成它们，且不重复。我们生成的每个数都能与一个整数配对。如果两者之间存在一一对应，也就是说，列表中的每个实数都能匹配一个整数，那就意味着可数集和不可数集大小相同。但我们做不到。

cues.en: Even though this list goes on forever, forever isn't enough. Watch this. If we go diagonally down our endless list of real numbers and take the first decimal of the first number and the second of the second number, the third of the third, and so on, and add one to each, subtracting one, if it happens to be a nine, we can generate a new real number.
cues.zh: 尽管这个列表永远延续，但永远也不够。看好了。如果我们沿着无尽实数列表斜向下走，取第一个数的第一位小数、第二个数的第二位小数、第三个数的第三位小数，依此类推，然后给每一位加一；如果刚好是 9，就减一，这样就能生成一个新的实数。

cues.en: that is obviously between 0 and 1, but since we've defined it to be different from every number on our endless list and at least one place, it's clearly not contained in the list. In other words, we've used up every single whole number, the entire infinity of them, and yet we can still come up with more real numbers. Here's something else that is true but counterintuitive.
cues.zh: 它显然在 0 和 1 之间，但由于我们已定义它在至少一位上与无尽列表中的每个数都不同，所以它显然不在列表里。换句话说，我们已经用光了每一个整数，用光了它们整个无穷，却仍然能构造出更多实数。还有一件真实但反直觉的事。

cues.en: There are the same number of even numbers as there are even and odd numbers. At first, that sounds ridiculous. Clearly there are only half as many even numbers as all whole numbers, but that intuition is wrong. The set of all whole numbers is denser, but every even number can be matched with a whole number. You will never run out of members of either set, so this one-to-one correspondence shows that both sets
cues.zh: 偶数的数量，和偶数加奇数的数量一样多。乍一听很荒谬。显然偶数只有所有整数的一半，但这种直觉是错的。所有整数的集合更稠密，但每个偶数都能与一个整数匹配。两个集合的成员都永远用不完，所以这种一一对应表明，这两个集合

cues.en: are the same size. In other words, infinity divided by 2 is still infinity. Infinity plus 1 is also infinity. A good illustration of this is Hilbert's paradox of the Grand Hotel. Imagine a hotel with a countably infinite number of rooms, but now imagine that there is a person booked into every single room. Seemingly, it's fully booked, right?
cues.zh: 大小相同。换句话说，无穷除以 2 仍是无穷。无穷加 1 也还是无穷。Hilbert 的 Grand Hotel 悖论是一个很好的例子。想象一家有可数无穷多个房间的酒店，但现在想象每个房间都住进了一位客人。看起来它已经客满了，对吧？

cues.en: No. Infinite sets go against common sense. You see, if a new guest shows up and wants a room, all the hotel has to do is move the guest in room number one to room number two. And the guest in room two to room three and three to four and four to five and so on, because the number of rooms is never-ending, we cannot run out of rooms. Infinity minus one is also infinity again.
cues.zh: 不。无限集合违背常识。你看，如果来了位新客人想要一个房间，酒店只需把 1 号房的客人移到 2 号房，把 2 号房的客人移到 3 号房，3 号移到 4 号，4 号移到 5 号，依此类推。因为房间数量永无止境，我们不可能用完房间。无穷减 1 又还是无穷。

cues.en: If one guest leaves the hotel, we can shift every guest the other way. Guest two goes to room one, three to two, four to three, and so on. Because we have an infinite amount of guests that is a never-ending supply of them, no room will be left empty. As it turns out, you can subtract any finite number from infinity and still be left with infinity. It doesn't care. It's unending.
cues.zh: 如果有一位客人离开酒店，我们可以把所有客人往反方向挪。2号客人去1号房，3号去2号，4号去3号，以此类推。因为我们有无穷无尽的客人，也就是取之不尽的客源，所以没有任何房间会空出来。事实证明，你可以从无穷中减去任何有限的数字，剩下的依然是无穷。它根本不在乎，因为它是永无止境的。

cues.en: Banach-Tarski hasn't left our sights yet. All of this is related. We are now ready to move on to shapes. Hilbert's hotel can be applied to a circle. Points around the circumference can be thought of as guests. If we remove one point from the circle, that point is gone, right? Infinity tells us it doesn't matter. The circumference of a circle is irrational. It's the radius times 2 pi.
cues.zh: 我们还没偏离巴拿赫-塔斯基定理（Banach-Tarski），这一切都是相关的。现在我们可以转向几何形状了。希尔伯特旅馆也可以应用在一个圆上。圆周上的点可以被看作是客人。如果我们从圆上移走一个点，那个点就消失了，对吧？但无穷告诉我们这无所谓。圆的周长是个无理数，等于半径乘以2π。

cues.en: So if we mark off points beginning from the hole, every radius length along the circumference going clockwise, we will never land on the same point twice. Ever. We can count off each point we mark with a whole number. So this set is never ending, but countable, just like guests in rooms in Hilbert's hotel. And like those guests, even though one has checked out, we can just shift the rest, move them
cues.zh: 所以，如果我们从那个缺口开始，顺时针方向沿着圆周每隔一个半径长度做一个标记点，我们就永远不会落在同一个点上两次。永远不会。我们可以用整数来计数标记的每一个点。因此这个集合是无穷无尽的，但又是可数的，就像希尔伯特旅馆房间里的客人一样。而且就像那些客人一样，即便有一位已经退房，我们只需把剩下的平移，将它们

cues.en: counterclockwise, and every room will be filled. Point one moves to fill in the hole, point two fills in the place where point one used to be, three fills in two, and so on. Since we have an unending supply of numbered points, no hole will be left unfilled. The missing point is forgotten. We apparently never needed it to be complete.
cues.zh: 逆时针移动，每个房间就都会被填满。1号点移动去填补那个空缺，2号点填补1号点原来的位置，3号填补2号，依此类推。既然我们有源源不断的编号点，就不会留下任何未填补的空缺。缺失的那个点就被遗忘了。显然，为了让它完整，我们从来都不需要那个点。

cues.en: There's one last neato consequence of infinity we should discuss before tackling Banach-Tarski. Ian Stewart famously proposed a brilliant dictionary, one that he called the Hyperwebster. The Hyperwebster lists every single possible word of any length formed from the 26 letters in the English alphabet. It begins with A followed by AA
cues.zh: 在着手解决巴拿赫-塔斯基悖论之前，我们还应该讨论无穷带来的最后一个奇妙结论。Ian Stewart曾提出过一本著名的绝妙词典，他称之为超级韦氏词典（Hyperwebster）。这本超级韦氏词典列出了由26个英文字母组成的所有可能、任意长度的单词。它以A开头，接着是AA，

cues.en: then AAA, then AAAA, and after an infinite number of those, AB, then ABA, then ABAA, ABAAA, and so on until Z. ZA, ZAA, etc. etc. until the final entry, an infinite sequence of Zs. Such a dictionary would contain every single word. Nay? Every single thought, definition, description.
cues.zh: 然后是AAA，接着是AAAA，在无限个A之后是AB，然后是ABA，接着是ABAA、ABAAA，依此类推直到Z。接着是ZA、ZAA等等，直到最后一项，即无限个Z的序列。这样一本词典将包含每一个词汇。不仅如此，它还包含每一个想法、定义和描述。

cues.en: Truth, lie, name, story, what happened to Amelia Earhart would be in that dictionary as well as every single thing that didn't happen to Amelia Earhart. Everything that could be said using our alphabet. Obviously, it would be huge, but the company publishing it might realize that they could take a shortcut. If they put all the words that begin with A in a volume titled A,
cues.zh: 无论是真相、谎言、名字还是故事，Amelia Earhart遭遇了什么都会在这本词典里，同样，任何她没经历过的事情也都在里面。所有能用我们这套字母表达的东西都在其中。显然，它会极其庞大，但出版它的公司可能会发现他们可以走个捷径。如果他们把所有以A开头的单词放在一本名为《A》的分册中，

cues.en: they wouldn't have to print the initial A. Readers would know to just add the A because it's the A volume. By removing the initial A, the publisher is left with every A word sans the first A, which has surprisingly become every possible word. Just one of the 26 volumes has been decomposed into the entire thing. It is now that we're ready to investigate this video's titular paradox.
cues.zh: 他们就不用印开头的那个字母A了。读者自然知道只要加上A就行，因为这是A分册。通过去掉开头的A，出版社手里的所有A字头单词就都去掉了首字母A，令人惊讶的是，这竟然变成了所有可能存在的单词。仅仅26个分册中的一本，就被分解成了整部词典。现在，我们终于准备好深入探究本期视频标题中的那个悖论了。

cues.en: What if we turned an object, a 3D thing, into a HyperWebster? Could we decompose pieces of it into the whole thing? Yes. The first thing we need to do is give every single point on the surface of the sphere one name and one name only. A good way to do this is to name them after how they can be reached by a given starting point. If we move this starting point across the surface of the sphere in steps that are just the right length,
cues.zh: 如果我们把一个物体，一个三维的东西，变成一个 HyperWebster，会怎样？我们能把它的碎片分解重组为整体吗？可以。我们需要做的第一件事，是给球面上的每一个点一个名字，而且只给一个名字。一个好办法是，按照从某个给定起点到达它们的方式来命名。如果我们让这个起点以恰好合适的步长在球面上移动，

cues.en: no matter how many times or in what direction we rotate so long as we never backtrack it will never wind up in the same place twice. We only need to rotate in four directions to achieve this paradox up, down, left, and right around two perpendicular axes. We are going to need every single possible sequence that can be made of any finite length out of just these four rotations. That means we will need left,
cues.zh: 无论旋转多少次、朝哪个方向旋转，只要从不回头，它就不会两次落到同一个地方。我们只需要绕两条垂直轴，朝上、下、左、右四个方向旋转，就能实现这个悖论。我们需要仅由这四种旋转构成的、任意有限长度的所有可能序列。这意味着我们需要左、

cues.en: right, up, and down, as well as left-left, left-up, left-down, but of course not left-right because, well, that's backtracking, going left and then right means you're the same as you were before you did anything. So, no left-rights, no right-lefts, and no up-downs, and no down-ups. Also, notice that I'm writing the rotations in order right to left.
cues.zh: 右、上、下，以及左左、左上、左下，当然不包括左右，因为那是在回头；先左再右意味着你回到什么都没做之前的状态。所以，不能有左右、右左、上下、下上。另外注意，我是按从右到左的顺序写这些旋转的。

cues.en: so the final rotation is the leftmost letter. That will be important later on. Anyway, a list of all possible sequences of allowed rotations that are finite in length is, well, huge. Countably infinite, in fact. But if we apply each one of them to a starting point, in green here, and then name the point we land on after the sequence that brought us there, we can name a countably infinite set of points on the surface.
cues.zh: 所以最后一次旋转是最左边的字母。这一点后面会很重要。总之，所有允许的、有限长度旋转序列的列表，嗯，非常庞大。事实上是可数无限的。但如果我们把其中每一个都作用到一个起点，这里用绿色标出，然后用带我们到达那里的序列来命名落点，我们就能命名球面上的一个可数无限点集。

cues.en: Let's look at how, say, these four strings on our list would work. Right up left. Okay, rotating the starting point this way takes us here. Let's color code the point based on the final rotation in its string. In this case it's left and for that we will use purple. Next up, down down. That sequence takes us here. We name the point DD and color it blue since we ended with a down rotation.
cues.zh: 来看看，比如我们列表上的这四个字符串会怎样运作。右、上、左。好，按这种方式旋转起点会带我们到这里。我们根据字符串中最后一次旋转来给这个点标色。这里最后是左，所以我们用紫色。下一个，下下。这个序列带我们到这里。我们把这个点命名为 DD，并涂成蓝色，因为最后是向下旋转。

cues.en: RDR, that will be this point's name, takes us here. And for a final right rotation, let's use red. Finally, for a sequence that ends with up, let's color-code the point orange. Now, if we imagine completing this process for every single sequence, we will have a countably infinite number of points named and color-coded. That's great, but not enough.
cues.zh: RDR 会作为这个点的名字，它带我们到这里。最后一次是向右旋转的，我们用红色。最后，对于以向上结尾的序列，我们把这个点标成橙色。现在，如果我们想象对每一个序列都完成这个过程，我们就会有可数无限个已命名并标好颜色的点。这很好，但还不够。

cues.en: there are an uncountably infinite number of points on a sphere's surface. But no worries, we can just pick a point we missed, any point, and color it green, making it a new starting point, and then run every sequence from here. After doing this, to an uncountably infinite number of starting points, we will have indeed named and colored every single point on the surface just once.
cues.zh: 球面上有不可数无限个点。但别担心，我们可以随便挑一个漏掉的点，任何点都行，把它涂成绿色，作为新的起点，然后从这里跑遍每一个序列。对不可数无限个起点都这样做之后，我们就确实把球面上的每一个点都恰好命名并着色了一次。

cues.en: with the exception of poles. Every sequence has two poles of rotation, locations on the sphere that come back to exactly where they started. For any sequence of right or left rotations, the poles are the north and south poles. The problem with poles like these is that more than one sequence can lead us to them. They can be named more than once and be colored in more than one color.
cues.zh: 但极点除外。每个序列都有两个旋转极点，也就是球面上转完后回到原处的位置。对于任何仅由向右或向左旋转组成的序列，其极点就是南北两极。这类极点的问题在于，不止一个序列可以通向它们。它们可能被多次命名，并被涂上不止一种颜色。

cues.en: For example, if you follow some other sequence to the North or South Pole, any subsequent rights or lefts will be equally valid names. In order to deal with this, we're going to just count them out of normal scheme and color them all yellow. Every sequence has two, so there are a countably infinite amount of them. Now, with every point on the sphere given just one name and just one of six colors, we are ready to take the entire sphere apart.
cues.zh: 例如，如果你顺着其他序列到达了北极或南极，那么之后无论再怎么向右或向左转，都会对应同样有效的名字。为了解决这个问题，我们干脆把它们排除在常规方案之外，全部涂成黄色。每个序列有两个极点，所以极点总共有可数无穷多个。现在，球面上的每个点都只有一个名字，且只对应六种颜色中的一种，我们就可以把整个球面拆开了。

cues.en: Every point on the surface corresponds to a unique line of points below it all the way to the center point, and we will be dragging every point's line along with it. The lone center point we will set aside. Okay, first we cut out and extract all the yellow poles, the green starting points, the orange up points, the blue down points, and the red and purple left and right points.
